item.title: [ 49] Xorg might as well not exist as a dedicated display server. Basically all of wh
item.description:
Xorg might as well not exist as a dedicated display server. Basically all of what made X11 into what it is has been abstracted to the point of meaninglessness. Mouse input is shared with Wayland through libinput. Keyboard input is shared with Wayland through XKB. Video output is shared with Wayland through DRM. Rasterization is shared with Wayland through EGL. All that remains is a bunch of thin wrapping separating the two.
X11 is already dead, we just don't know it yet.

item.title: [ 48] Mandami fulfills another campaign promise by disbanding divisive NYPD unit
item.description:
https://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/local/mamdani-tisch-disband-nypd-strategic-response-group/6572816/

Mayor Zohran Mamdani and NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch have agreed to disband the police department's Strategic Response Group, a specialized unit critics say is too militaristic when it comes to handling mass protests, but one others argue is essential to counter-terrorism operations.

Mamdani has repeatedly said he doesn't believe terrorism duties and responses to First Amendment-related incidents should fall under one unit, and he made disbanding the unit a key pledge of his 2025 mayoral campaign. Under the plan rolled out Monday, those two priorities — counter-terror and protest-related duties — will be decoupled. Counter-terror duties move under the NYPD's Intelligence and Counterterrorism Bureau.

Starting in the new year, the city will restructure its response to protests through the creation of a civilian-led Community Dialogue and De-escalation Division (CDDD). That group, created within the Mayor's Office of Community Safety, will not have weapons or arrest powers, Mamdani said in Monday's announcement.

“New Yorkers exercising their constitutional right to protest should not be met with the same police response as a terrorism threat. We are establishing a new, civilian-led approach that prioritizes dialogue, engagement and de-escalation," Mamdani said in a statement.

The mayor said it was part of "building a new approach to public safety."

To support that civilian-led group, the NYPD is creating a First Amendment Support Team (FAST) made of 30 officers trained in communication and de-escalation. FAST will lead those efforts until the new civlian-led team is established.

item.title: [ 67] Breaking News: FAA Orders Nationwide Ground Stop for All Airports
item.description:
Thread theme: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yLHCm7e0uBg

> https://abcnews.com/US/nationwide-ground-stop-ordered-airports-faa/story?id=138121848

The Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop Friday for all airports due to a communication issue affecting air traffic control.

The agency's alert said the stop was "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety."

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in an X statement a short while later that the stop was "due a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers."

"FAA technicians are investigating the issue," he said in an X post.

This is the second time since Sept. 11, 2001, that the FAA has ordered a nationwide ground stop. The last time was in 2023, when the FAA NOTAM system went down and pilots could not get their pre-departure paperwork.

Air Route Traffic Control Centers are responsible for all flights above 18,000 feet. There are 22 of those centers in the U.S.

Pilots who are in the air have flight plans and are prepared to continue with their flight path in case of such an emergency, according to ABC News contributor John Nance.

"All pilots in that environment know what to do," Nance told ABC News on Friday.

"It is a matter of predictability. Air Traffic Control knows that airplane is going to come out of the sky at some point of time looking for a pathway," he later added.

Earlier in the afternoon, the FAA issued a ground stop at both Chicago's O'Hare and Midway airports due to equipment outage.

>This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

item.title: [ 45] ‘Bring Back THE Boss’: Nvidia Employees Petition for Jensen Huang’s Return
item.description:
https://www.wired.com/story/nvidia-employees-petition-for-jensen-huangs-return/

Some Nvidia employees are calling for Jensen Huang’s return even after his multiple reported extramarital affairs and abrupt resignation, according to internal correspondence reviewed by WIRED.

An internal “suggestion box” post submitted before Huang’s resignation by a longtime engineer at Nvidia urged the company’s board to take employee sentiment into consideration prior to taking any action. The submission has attracted more than 1,600 comments since then, with several asking board members to find a way to bring back Huang.

“If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss,” wrote one anonymous commenter.

“We are all humans and can make mistakes. Jensen did so many good things and he needs a second chance,” wrote another.

One employee went as far as sending a companywide email demanding transparency into Huang’s exit. “I stand by Jensen,” the staffer wrote. “Not because I believe any person is infallible, but because I refuse to believe that standing for fairness must mean standing at a distance from someone whose leadership has meant so much to us.”

The employee couldn’t be reached for comment, while the engineer behind the suggestion box post declined to comment.

Nvidia and its new board chair, investor Harvey Jones, didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.
